meta.title: Northline — a small studio for careful work
meta.description: Northline is a two-person studio that designs and builds websites meant to last a decade.

site.name: Northline
site.tagline: Built by hand, kept in git.

hero.title: A small studio for careful work.
hero.subtitle: We make websites for people who intend to keep them — plain HTML, honest typography, and no machinery you have to feed every quarter.

work.title: Selected work
work.intro: Three projects that show the range: an archive, a shop, and a site that is mostly one very good page.

projects.title: Fenwick Press
projects.summary: Three hundred back-catalogue titles rebuilt as a fast static archive, with a small shop attached.

projects.title: Merrow & Co.
projects.summary: An identity and one-page site for a cabinet shop that had been running on a phone number and word of mouth.

projects.title: The Tuesday Letter
projects.summary: A weekly essay list moved off a rented platform and onto its own archive, feed included.

studio.title: How we work
studio.body: Two people, one project at a time, start to finish. We write the HTML by hand, keep the page weight under a couple of hundred kilobytes, and hand over a repository you own outright. When the work is done you can edit the site yourself, from a laptop or a phone, without calling us.
services: Website design and hand-built front ends
Quiet ongoing care — small changes, same week

contact.title: Start a conversation
contact.body: Tell us what you are making and roughly when it needs to exist. We answer every note, and we will say so plainly if we are not the right studio for it.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.body: That page is not here. It may have been renamed — every rename here leaves a redirect, so this one is probably a typo.
